mineboost.lock.off_entityculling_already: Off: EntityCulling already hides entities you can't see.
mineboost.lock.off_entityculling_is_inst: Off: EntityCulling is installed and already hides things behind walls.

mineboost.lock.off_with_iris_shader_pack: Off with Iris: shader packs draw mobs their own way.
mineboost.memory.copied: Copied. Paste it into your launcher: Installations > Edit > More options > JVM arguments.
mineboost.memory.igpu: and with integrated graphics the rest of the RAM is also your video memory.
mineboost.memory.may_use: Minecraft may use up to %.1f GB now.
mineboost.memory.pc_ram: This PC has %.1f GB of RAM. Minecraft may use up to %.1f GB now.
mineboost.memory.recommended: Recommended: %s GB. More isn't faster: Java then cleans up less often but for longer (stutters),
mineboost.memory.too_little: You give it less than recommended: copy the line below into your launcher.
mineboost.memory.too_much: You give it more than needed: lowering it can reduce stutters.
mineboost.option.animated_textures.toolt: Turn off to freeze water, lava, fire and portal animations. Small boost.
mineboost.option.background_fps.impact: None while you play. Frees your PC while Minecraft is in the background.
mineboost.option.background_fps.tooltip: FPS limit when Minecraft isn't the window you're using (alt-tab). Minimized always drops to 1 FPS. Frees your PC for OBS, Discord or your browser.
mineboost.option.block_entity_distance.i: Small: +2% with 40 chests in view. Worth it only in big storage rooms.
mineboost.option.block_entity_distance.t: Chests, signs, banners, heads and beds farther than this aren't drawn. Great for big bases and storage rooms.
mineboost.option.disable_particles.impac: None normally. Big during explosions and in particle-heavy places.
mineboost.option.disable_particles.toolt: No particles at all: no explosions, smoke, block breaking or potion swirls. Stronger than vanilla's Particles: Minimal.
mineboost.option.dynamic_render_scale.im: Holds your FPS target by trading sharpness for FPS only when needed.
mineboost.option.dynamic_render_scale.to: Dynamic Render Scale: lowers the scale by itself when you're below your FPS Target (60 if off) and raises it back (up to Render Scale) when there's FPS to spare. Changes at most once a second.
mineboost.option.entity_distance.impact: High in crowds: +30% FPS at 24 blocks (measured with 98 mobs 26-44 blocks away).
mineboost.option.entity_distance.tooltip: Mobs, animals, items and item frames farther than this aren't drawn. One of the biggest boosts near farms and mob grinders.
mineboost.option.far_entity_ticks.impact: None measured (−2%) with 300 mobs behind you; experimental. Off by default.
mineboost.option.far_entity_ticks.toolti: Experimental: mobs more than 48 blocks away and behind you are animated only every 4th tick on your side. The world still runs them normally.
mineboost.option.far_mob_detail.impact: High with armored mobs: +31% FPS and +48% 1% low at 16 blocks (measured with 98 mobs in armor).
mineboost.option.far_mob_detail.tooltip: Simple Far Mobs: mobs farther than this are drawn without armor, held items, saddles, heads and other extra layers (each one draws the mob again). Sheep wool, glowing eyes and charged creepers are kept, and players always look normal.
mineboost.option.fps_overlay.tooltip: Show FPS, average FPS and 1% low in the top-right corner. The 1% low tells you how bad the stutters are.
mineboost.option.fps_target.impact: High when you're below the target: render distance is the biggest FPS cost in Minecraft.
mineboost.option.fps_target.tooltip: Smart Render Distance. Pick the FPS you want: when the game drops below it, MineBoost lowers the render distance, and raises it again (up to the distance you chose) when there's FPS to spare.
mineboost.option.frame_graph.impact: Tiny (a few small rectangles per frame).
mineboost.option.frame_graph.tooltip: A small graph of the last 100 frame times under the FPS Overlay. Tall red bars are stutters.
mineboost.option.hide_beacon_beams.toolt: Don't draw beacon beams (the beacon still works).
mineboost.option.hide_decorations.impact: Medium in bases full of armor stands and item frames.
mineboost.option.hide_decorations.toolti: Don't draw armor stands, item frames and paintings. Helps in decorated bases and villages.
mineboost.option.hide_name_tags.impact: Small, only with many named mobs or players.
mineboost.option.hide_name_tags.tooltip: Don't draw names above players and named mobs.
mineboost.option.hide_sky.tooltip: Don't draw the sky, sun, moon and stars. The background is just the fog colour.
mineboost.option.hide_vignette.impact: Tiny (about one full-screen layer less per frame).
mineboost.option.hide_vignette.tooltip: Don't draw the dark shading around the edges of the screen. A small saving, and a clearer view.
mineboost.option.hide_weather.impact: Medium while it rains or snows (none in clear weather).
mineboost.option.hide_weather.tooltip: Don't draw rain and snow. It still rains (crops grow, fire goes out); you just don't see it.
mineboost.option.idle_fps.impact: None while you play. Saves power and heat when you're away, so a laptop doesn't slow down from heat later.
mineboost.option.idle_fps.tooltip: Idle Mode: when you haven't touched the keyboard or mouse for a while (see Idle After), limit the FPS to this. Anything you press brings full FPS back instantly. Your laptop stays cooler, so it doesn't slow down from heat later.
mineboost.option.idle_seconds.tooltip: How long without input before Idle Mode starts.
mineboost.option.impostors.tooltip: Impostors: mobs farther than this are drawn as a flat picture of themselves that turns towards you, instead of the full model with armor and items. They don't animate, so use it for far mobs only. Players, bosses and glowing mobs are always drawn normally.
mineboost.option.item_distance.impact: Medium near lots of drops: +10% FPS at 6 blocks (measured with 150 stacks on the ground).
mineboost.option.item_distance.tooltip: Dropped items farther than this aren't drawn (normally Minecraft draws them up to about 16 blocks). Farms and explosions leave lots of them around.
mineboost.option.max_entities.impact: High in crowds: +37% FPS at 50 (measured with 250 mobs and items in view).
mineboost.option.max_entities.tooltip: Draw only this many of the closest mobs, animals and items. Huge help at farms and mob grinders. Players, bosses and glowing mobs are always drawn.
mineboost.option.max_sounds.impact: Only with very many sounds at once; couldn't be measured on the test PC (no audio).
mineboost.option.max_sounds.tooltip: Most sounds playing at once. Huge farms and explosions can play hundreds.
mineboost.option.menu_fps.impact: None while you play. Your PC runs cooler while a menu is open.
mineboost.option.menu_fps.tooltip: FPS limit while an inventory, chest or the pause menu is open. Nothing there needs full speed, so your PC runs cooler and quieter. (Chat isn't limited.)
mineboost.option.particle_limit.impact: None normally. Big during TNT, potion clouds and particle farms (stops the FPS crash).
mineboost.option.particle_limit.tooltip: Most particles on screen at once. Stops TNT, big farms and potion clouds from tanking your FPS, while normal particles still show.
mineboost.option.particle_range.impact: Small normally. Helps when far-away explosions, rain or farms make lots of particles.
mineboost.option.particle_range.tooltip: Particles farther away than this aren't created at all. Rain splashes, far-away explosions and farms make lots you can barely see.
mineboost.option.render_scale.impact: High when the graphics card is the limit (integrated graphics): +15% at 50% and +17% at 75% on our test PC. Run the A/B test to see yours.
mineboost.option.render_scale.tooltip: Render Scale: draw the world at a lower resolution and stretch it to the window. The HUD, text and menus stay sharp. 75% means about half the pixels to fill, which is what slows down integrated graphics the most.
mineboost.option.render_scale_filter.too: How Render Scale stretches the picture: ON = Nearest (sharp pixels, a bit faster), OFF = Linear (smooth).
mineboost.option.render_scale_min.toolti: The lowest scale Dynamic Render Scale may go down to.
mineboost.option.render_scale_sharpen.im: None by itself; costs about 9 texture reads per pixel while Render Scale is on (measured below).
mineboost.option.render_scale_sharpen.to: Sharpen (CAS) for Render Scale: makes the smaller picture look crisp again, without halos around edges. Only used while Render Scale is below 100%.
mineboost.option.section_culling.impact: None measured (−7%, within noise): Smart Culling already hides the same mobs. Off by default.
mineboost.option.section_culling.tooltip: Section Culling: the game already knows which chunk sections you can't see (caves under you, behind hills) but still draws the mobs in them. This skips those mobs.
mineboost.option.simple_items.impact: Small: +4% with 150 stacks on the ground.
mineboost.option.simple_items.tooltip: Draw a stack of dropped items as one item instead of a pile of up to five. Up to 5x less to draw for every dropped stack.
mineboost.option.smart_culling.impact: High in caves, villages and bases where walls hide mobs and chests; none in open fields.
mineboost.option.smart_culling.tooltip: Don't draw mobs, items, chests and signs that are completely hidden behind solid blocks. Big boost in caves, villages and bases. Glass and leaves never hide anything, and things close to you are always drawn.
mineboost.option.smooth_fog.tooltip: Smooth Fog Edge: fog starts earlier so chunks at the edge of your render distance fade in instead of popping. Good with Smart Render Distance.
mineboost.option.spike_log.tooltip: Note every frame slower than 50 ms, with what was going on (see Tools > Last report & spikes, and config/minemeboost/spikes.log).
mineboost.preset.balanced.desc: Good looks and smooth FPS on most PCs.
mineboost.preset.high.desc: Close to Minecraft's defaults, a bit farther. For decent PCs.
mineboost.preset.intel_igpu.desc: Made for laptops with Intel UHD / Iris graphics (like an i3 or i5 with UHD). Turns off what costs integrated graphics the most (menu blur, clouds, Fancy leaves, shadows), keeps smooth lighting and 8 chunks so it still looks good.
mineboost.preset.low.desc: Big FPS boost that still looks like Minecraft.
mineboost.preset.potato.desc: Maximum FPS for very weak PCs. Looks rough: short view distance, no particles, no rain.
mineboost.preset.toaster.desc: The absolute minimum: 2 chunk view distance, nothing extra drawn. For PCs that can barely run Minecraft.
mineboost.preset.ultra.desc: Everything turned up, long view distance. For strong PCs.
mineboost.profiles.no_code: No MineBoost profile code (MBB1:...) in the clipboard
mineboost.render_scale.fabulous: Not available with Fabulous graphics. Use Fancy or Fast.
mineboost.render_scale.iris: Not available with Iris (shaders have their own resolution settings).
mineboost.screen.other_fps_counter: Another FPS counter is on. Turn it off first.
mineboost.text.about_6_minutes_each_boos: About 6 minutes: each boost off and on, twice. Stand still looking at a busy spot. The table goes to config/minemeboost/benchmark-results.md. Send it to compare PCs!
mineboost.text.another_preset_in_the_net: Another preset in the Nether, underground, near crowds or on an elytra.
mineboost.text.closes_the_menu_and_measu: Closes the menu and measures your FPS for 10 seconds. Keep playing normally; the result shows up in chat. Try it with different presets!
mineboost.text.closes_the_menu_and_tries: Closes the menu and tries the presets from Ultra down (about 7 seconds each), then keeps the best looking one that reaches your FPS Target (or 60 FPS if that's off). Keep playing normally while it runs.
mineboost.text.for_playing_on_battery_30: For playing on battery: 30 FPS, Render Scale at most 70%%, at most 500 particles. Also on a key (Controls > MineBoost).
mineboost.text.is_the_fastest_but_only_r: is the fastest, but only reached %s FPS (target %s)
mineboost.text.lag_doctor_a_b_test_of: Lag Doctor, A/B test of every boost, memory and JVM advice, context rules, FPS profiles and Battery Saver.
mineboost.text.leaving_a_situation_puts_: Leaving a situation puts your own settings back. Now: %s
mineboost.text.mineboost_a_b_done_best_o: MineBoost A/B done. Best on your PC: %s. Full table: config/minemeboost/benchmark-results.md
mineboost.text.name: Name
mineboost.text.no_report_yet_press_run_t: No report yet: press Run, then play normally for 30 seconds.
mineboost.text.play_normally_for_30_seco: Play normally for 30 seconds; then it shows what costs you the most FPS, with a Fix button for each.
mineboost.text.recent_spikes_frames_over: Recent spikes (frames over 50 ms), also in config/minemeboost/spikes.log:
mineboost.text.s_was_disabled_because_of: %s was disabled because of an error
